Democracy Defender Mod Manager (DDMM), release candidate 20: *your mods, your democracy, defended.* It's still an
early build, but it's meant to be usable by anyone, not just developers.

**The DDMM Promise, in brief:** every mod is welcome (DDMM never blocks, blacklists or ranks mods or mod sites),
no account is ever needed on any site, your files stay in a folder you control, it's Apache-2.0 open source
forever, and update checks never run unless you ask.

## Quick start

1. **Download** the right file for you (see the table below).
2. **Run it.** DDMM looks for your Helldivers 2 install automatically. If Steam is in its usual place, there's
   nothing to set up.
3. **Add mods and click Deploy.** Drag in an archive or folder, or click "Add URL" and paste a link.

**Works with AyakaMods, Nexus Mods, ModWorkshop, GameBanana, GitHub, any direct link, or files already on your
disk.** Special love to the AyakaMods community ❤️, one of the best homes for Helldivers 2 modding. Go say hi:
<https://ayakamods.com/games/helldivers-2.119/>.

## Which file do I download?

| You want... | Download |
| --- | --- |
| A normal install on Windows (Start Menu shortcut, uninstaller) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.20-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows without installing anything (unzip and run) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.20-windows-x64-portable.zip` |
| Linux: Fedora, Nobara, openSUSE (`dnf`/`zypper`) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.20-linux-x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux: Debian, Ubuntu, Mint (`apt`) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.20-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux: other distros, no install (uses your desktop's graphics libraries) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.20-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: Arch/CachyOS, or just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.20-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

Linux install commands, the dependencies for each distro, and fixes for a blank window or AppImage/FUSE errors
are in [Installing on Linux](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/getting-started/linux/).

**One-click install (optional):** also grab the browser extension: `ddmm-extension-chrome-1.0.1.zip`
(Chrome, Edge, Brave) or `ddmm-extension-firefox-1.0.1.zip` (Firefox). See
[One-click install](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/using/one-click-install/).

Check `SHA256SUMS.txt` if you want to verify your download.

## What's new in 2.0.0-rc.20

### Crash safety

If DDMM is closed or crashes partway through an update or a Replace, the next start now finishes the profile
changes, or keeps the old version. Before, the mod's entries in your profiles could be left pointing at an ID no mod
has, and showed as "Mod not found".

- **You get one of two results:** either the old version is back with your profiles as they were, or the new
  version is in place with its profile entries kept, moved to the new ID where the update changes it, and option
  choices that no longer fit reset to the defaults.
- **It covers every way of replacing a mod:** updates, Replace when you add, drop or Add URL a file, the browser
  extension, and Replace in the import checklist.
- **The one exception is unchanged:** if a mod's author changes its ID in an update, the old entries still show
  as "Mod not found", crash or not. Add the updated mod to the profile again, then remove the old entry.
- **If profiles.json can't be written** at that start (another program has it open), DDMM tries again on the next
  start.
- Option choices reset this way aren't announced with the usual *options reset* message, so check the mod's
  options after such a crash.

See [Updating mods](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/using/updating-mods/#after-updating-redeploy).

### Mods packed in a folder

Some mods have their files inside an extra folder (`My Mod/My Mod v1.2/manifest.json` instead of
`My Mod/manifest.json`).

- **Add Folder on a folder that's already in DDMM's mod storage** now unwraps it in place, the same way as when
  the mod comes in an archive: DDMM uses the author's `manifest.json`, so the mod gets the author's ID and options.
  Before, DDMM generated its own manifest and turned the inner folders into options.
  - Anything else next to the inner folder (a readme, a picture) is **moved into the mod's folder**, because it's
    your only copy. If one of those has the same name as something in the mod's folder, the folder is refused and
    nothing is moved.
  - If DDMM closes partway through, the next start finishes the move or puts the folder back as it was.
- **Patch files next to the extra folder:** DDMM installs everything as before, with the top as the mod, and now
  warns that the folder's `manifest.json` wasn't used. Nothing is left out.
- **Archives:** a readme or picture next to the mod's folder is still not installed, as before. Your archive
  still has it.
- **Mods added this way by an older DDMM** are left as they are for now. They switch to the author's ID the next
  time they're updated, and their profile entries move with them.

See [Add Folder](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/using/adding-mods/#add-folder) and
[Zipping the folder or its contents](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/authors/packaging/#zipping-the-folder-or-its-contents).

### Maintenance

- **Updated libraries and build tools,** and removed three unused packages. One of them, the file-system plugin,
  had security fixes that didn't affect DDMM, because the app never had permission to use it.
- **Game-running detection does less work,** and old log files are now really cleaned up, so the log folder
  stays within its limit.

### If you're coming from rc.14 or earlier

If you used the Skip List with rc.14 or earlier, verify the game files in Steam once (Library → Helldivers 2 →
Properties → Installed Files → Verify integrity of game files). Older versions could delete the game's own files
for those names.

**Skipped a few?** rc.10 had important safety fixes, rc.11 fixed mod deletion, rc.12 fixed mod option dropdowns, rc.13 fixed AyakaMods update checks, rc.14 fixed the Mods page stuck on "Loading...", rc.15 fixed Deploy and Purge removing mods and game files, rc.16 added Replace for mods with the same ID, rc.17 was a security update for archive extraction, rc.18 fixed a rare memory bug on Linux and rc.19 added Move to Top/Bottom by priority, Escape for popups and Replace in Import; see the [releases page](https://github.com/katsyk/DemocracyDefenderModManager/releases).

Thanks to everyone testing the release candidates. o7

## Known limitations

- **Windows builds are unsigned.** Windows SmartScreen will likely show a warning the first time you run the
  installer or the app. Click **"More info" → "Run anyway"** to continue.
- **The Linux .rpm and .deb are unsigned**, so openSUSE needs `zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm`.
- **This is still a release candidate.** Expect some rough edges, and please report what you find.
